findings.issue: observedBySeat validates hands/vpip/pfr but not that `seat` is an integer seat number; a non-numeric seat is interpolated into the RangeError message and otherwise silently never matches.
findings.evidence: worker message `observed[i].seat` (sender is the same-origin main thread, not an external party) -> observedBySeat -> Map key / error text. No HTML sink: the error travels back as ok:false {name,message} data and no innerHTML/dangerouslySetInnerHTML exists in src. No reachable exploit.
findings.fix: Optional: also check Number.isInteger(seat) && seat >= 1 && seat <= 10 so malformed snapshots fail closed with a clear message.

summary: No BLOCKER or MAJOR issues. The new optional `observed` field on recommend/grade worker requests is validated by estimateOpponentRanges/observedBySeat (finite 0-100 percentages, non-negative integer hands, no duplicate seats; non-array ignored), and any throw (including TypeError from null entries) is caught by handleAdviceRequest and returned as ok:false, so it fails closed. The worker sender is the same-origin app, so the boundary is fault-tolerance rather than attacker-facing. applyUserAction stores a shallow per-entry copy of the snapshot (plain numbers), and reviewEntries regrades through the same validating path, so later persisted UserDecision data that is tampered with would surface as an exception from gradeView rather than unsafe behaviour (callers of reviewEntries should continue to treat that as an error). --check-advice is a local CLI flag with no file/shell/network sinks. No new dependencies, secrets, or security-relevant randomness.
